This indicates that the reward of the good among them is Paradise, in several respects:

First: "man" (min) is a word of generality, so it encompasses every one who fears.

Second: He ordered the mentioned reward upon fear of His standing, which shows that he deserves it by it. There has been disagreement over whether the idafah of "standing" to "Lord" is an idafah of the verbal noun to its subject or to its object, on two views: One is that the meaning is "and for him who fears his standing before his Lord," so on this it is an idafah of the verbal noun to its object.

The second is that the meaning is "and for him who fears the standing of his Lord over him and His watching over him," so it is an idafah of the verbal noun to its subject.

The two views are likewise in the words of the Exalted: ﴿But as for he who feared the standing of his Lord and restrained the soul from desire﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 40], and its parallel in His words: ﴿That is for him who fears My standing and fears My threat﴾ [Ibrahim: 14]. These are three places.

It may be said: The preferred one is the first, and that the meaning is "he feared his standing before his Lord," for several reasons:

One: The Qur'an's method in warning is to warn them of Allah and the Last Day. When He warns them of Him, He attaches the fear to Him, not to His standing over them, as in His words: ﴿So do not fear them, but fear Me﴾ [Al 'Imran: 175], and His words: ﴿That is for him who fears his Lord﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 8], and His words: ﴿They fear their Lord from above them﴾ [al-Nahl: 50], and His words: ﴿Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen, for them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [al-Mulk: 12]. In all of this He did not mention fear of His standing over them; rather He praised them for their fear and dread of Him.

Fear may also be mentioned attached to His punishment, as in His words: ﴿They hope for His mercy and fear His punishment﴾ [al-Isra': 57].

As for fear of His standing over them, although it is so, it is not the method of the Qur'an.

Two: This is parallel to His words: ﴿And warn with it those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 51]. Their fear of being gathered to Him is their fear of their standing before Him, and the Qur'an explains one part by another.

Three: The fear of a servant's standing before his Lord in the Hereafter is found only in one who believes in meeting Him, in the Last Day and in resurrection after death. This is what deserves the two mentioned gardens, for one does not believe in that with true belief except one who believes in the messengers, and it is from the belief in the unseen that the messengers brought.

As for Allah's standing over His servant in this world, His watching over him and His power over him, this is acknowledged by the believer and the disbeliever, the righteous and the wicked, and most of the disbelievers fear Allah's requital of them in this world, because they have witnessed the punishment of the wrongdoer for his wrong and the reward of the good for his goodness. But the servant's standing before his Lord in the Hereafter is not believed in except by the one who believes in the messengers.

If it is said: If the meaning is that he feared his Lord's standing over him in the Hereafter through requital, then both estimations are equal, so from where have you preferred one of them?

It is said: Warning with the servant's standing before his Lord is more forceful than warning with the Lord's standing over the servant, and for this He warned us in His words: ﴿The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 6]. Also, it is a specific standing, attributed to Allah, and that is on the Day of Resurrection, unlike Allah's standing over the servant, which is at every time. Moreover, Allah's power over the servant, His watching over him and His knowledge of him are not called "the standing of Allah," nor is this commonly used of the Lord.

Also, in the Qur'an and the Sunnah "maqam" is used only for a place, as in His words: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praised station﴾ [al-Isra': 79], and His words: ﴿How many gardens and springs and crops and a noble station did they leave behind﴾ [al-Dukhan: 25–26], and His words: ﴿Better in station and finer in assembly﴾ [Maryam: 73]. The point is that His words ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens﴾ encompass both categories, for several reasons, two of which were mentioned earlier:

Third: His words following this promise: ﴿Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾

Fourth: That He described their women as: ﴿Neither man nor jinn has touched them before them﴾ [al-Rahman: 56]. And this, Allah knows best, means that no man before them has touched the women of mankind, nor has any jinn before them touched the women of the jinn.

What shows that their reward is Paradise is His words: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—indeed, We do not allow to be lost the reward of one who does good work. Those will have gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow﴾ [al-Kahf: 30–31], and similar generalities.

It has been established that among them are believers, so they enter into the generality, just as their disbelievers enter among the disbelievers deserving the threat. The entry of their believers into the verses of promise is more fitting than the entry of their disbelievers into the verses of threat, for promise is His grace and threat is His justice, and His grace is from His mercy, which overcomes His wrath.

Also, the entry of their disobedient ones into the Fire was only because of their opposition to Allah's command; so when they obey Allah, they are admitted to Paradise. Also, there is no abode for the accountable other than Paradise and the Fire, and every accountable one who does not enter the Fire, Paradise is his abode.

Also, it has been established that when they answer the caller of Allah, He forgives them and protects them from His punishment, and everyone who is forgiven enters Paradise without doubt; the benefit of forgiveness is nothing but winning Paradise and being saved from the Fire. Also, it has been established that the Messenger was sent to them and that they are obligated to follow him, and that whoever of them obeys Allah and His Messenger is with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor, of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous, and excellent companions they are. As He said: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger—those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor, of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions﴾ [al-Nisa': 69]. He, glorified be He, has informed of His angels, the bearers of the Throne and those around it, that they seek forgiveness for those who believe, and that they say: ﴿So forgive those who repent and follow Your way and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire. Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them﴾ [Ghafir: 7–8].

This shows that every believer whom Allah forgives and whom He protects from the punishment of Hellfire has been promised Paradise. Belief, forgiveness of sin and protection from the Fire have been established for their believers, as mentioned, so their entry into Paradise is necessary, and Allah knows best.

And since their accountability has been established, with their division into Muslims, disbelievers, and righteous and below that, they are in the weighing in the manner of the human levels mentioned before, except that there is no messenger among them. The best of their ranks is the rank of the righteous, and if they had a higher rank than this, it would have been mentioned.

The Qur'an has indicated their division into three categories: righteous, those below them, and disbelievers.

Humankind surpasses them in the rank of messengership and prophethood, and the rank of those brought near, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 55, verse 46–47:

﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens.﴾

It has been said: he is the servant who desires disobedience, then recalls the standing of his Lord over him in this world and his standing before Him in the Hereafter, and so he leaves it for the sake of Allah.

(A subtle point)

Yahya ibn Ayyub said: In Madinah there was a young man whom ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) admired. One night, after the ʿIsha prayer, he went out, and a woman appeared before him and presented herself to him, and he was captivated by her, and she went off. He followed her until she stopped at her door, and he saw her, and his heart was stirred, and this verse came to his mind: ﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah, when an impulse from Satan touches them, remember [Allah], and at once they are seeing clearly.﴾

He fell unconscious. The woman looked at him, and he was like a corpse. She and a maidservant of hers kept helping each other with him until they laid him at the door of his house. His father came out and found him lying at the door of the house, afflicted. He carried him in and brought him in. He regained consciousness, and his father asked him, "What has befallen you, my son?" but he did not tell him. His father kept at him until he told him. When he recited the verse, he gave a gasp, and his soul departed. The news of his story reached ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him), and he said:

"Why did you not inform me of his death?" So he went until he stood at his grave and called out, "O so-and-so! ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens.﴾"

He heard a voice from within the grave: "My Lord has given me it, O ʿUmar."

Al-Hasan related this story from ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) in another form. He said: In the time of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) there was a young man who was constant in the mosque and in worship. A slave girl desired him, and he entertained the thought of her in his soul. Then he remembered and saw clearly, and he gave a gasp and fainted from it. His paternal uncle came and carried him to his house. When he regained consciousness he said, "O uncle, go to ʿUmar, convey my greetings to him, and say to him: what is the reward of one who fears the standing of his Lord?" The uncle informed ʿUmar, and he came to him, but he had died. Then ʿUmar said, "For you are two gardens."

In the Jami' of al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both), he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Dhu al-Kifl did not refrain from any sin he committed. A woman came to him, and he gave her sixty dinars on condition that he would lie with her. When he sat between her legs as a man sits with his wife, she trembled and wept. He said, 'Why are you weeping? Have I forced you?' She said, 'No, but this is an act I have never done, and only need drove me to it.' He said, 'Would you do this when you have never done it before?' Then he said, 'Go, and the dinars are yours.' Then he said, 'By Allah, Dhu al-Kifl will never disobey Allah again.' He died that same night, and in the morning it was written on his door: 'Allah has forgiven Dhu al-Kifl.'" Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan hadith.

Abu Hurayrah and Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave a sermon before his death, and in his sermon he said: "Whoever has the power over a woman or a slave girl unlawfully, and leaves her out of fear of Allah, Allah will grant him security on the Day of the Great Terror, will forbid him the Fire, and will admit him to Paradise."

Malik ibn Dinar said: The Gardens of Bliss lie between Firdaws and the Gardens of ʿAdn. In them are maidens created from the rose of Paradise. They are inhabited by those who were inclined toward sins, but when they remembered Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, they became watchful of Him, and their necks bent from fear of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Maymun ibn Mihran said: Remembrance is of two kinds. Remembering Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with the tongue is good, but better than it is that you remember Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, when you are about to commit His prohibitions.

Qatadah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: It has been related to us that the Prophet of Allah used to say: "No man is able to commit something forbidden and then leave it, out of nothing but fear of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, except that He will replace it for him in this world, before the Hereafter, with something better for him than that."

ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr said: The truthfulness of faith and its righteousness is that a man is alone with a beautiful woman and leaves her, leaving her only for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

(Section)

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ashʿari, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Two gardens of gold, their vessels and their adornments and what is in them; and two gardens of silver, their vessels and their adornments and what is in them; and nothing stands between the people and looking at their Lord except the cloak of greatness over His face, in the Garden of ʿAdn." And Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens﴾, and He mentioned them, then said ﴿and besides them two gardens﴾.

So these are four, and there has been disagreement about His words ﴿and besides them﴾: does it mean that they are above them, or below them?

On two opinions:

One group said: "besides them" means nearer to the Throne than them, so they would be above them.

Another group said: "Rather, the meaning of 'besides them' is below them."

They said: This is what is transmitted in the language of the Arabs when they say: "This is besides this," meaning it is lower in rank, as one of them said to someone who had exaggerated his praise:

"I am below what you say, and above what you have in your own mind."

In al-Sihah (of al-Jawhari): "dun" is the opposite of "fawq" (above).

It indicates falling short of the goal. Then he said: "It is said: this is dun that," meaning it is nearer to it.

The context indicates the preference of the first two gardens over them in ten respects:

First: His words ﴿with branches﴾ (dhawata afnan). Regarding it there are two views: one is that it is the plural of fanan, which is a branch; the second is that it is the plural of fann, which is a kind, meaning possessing various kinds of fruits and other things. This is not mentioned concerning the two that follow them.

Second: His words ﴿in them are two flowing springs﴾.

Concerning the latter two: "in them are two gushing springs." The nadkhah is the one that gushes, and the jariyah is the one that flows freely; the latter is better than the gushing one, for it includes both gushing and flowing.

Third: He said ﴿in them of every fruit are two kinds﴾, while concerning the latter two: ﴿in them are fruit, and palm trees, and pomegranates﴾. There is no doubt that the description of the first two is more complete.

The two kinds have been disputed, after agreement that they are two types. 

One group said: the two kinds are fresh and dried, the dried one not falling short in its excellence and quality of the fresh, and one enjoys it as one enjoys the dried.

There is a view here that is not hidden.

Another group said: the two kinds are a known type and a type of a different form.

Another group said: two types, and they did not add more; and the apparent, and Allah knows best, is that it is the sweet, the sour, the white and the red, for the variety of kinds of fruit is more wondrous, more appetizing, and more delightful to the eye and the mouth.

Fourth: He said ﴿reclining on carpets whose linings are of brocade﴾.

This is an indication of the excellence and high value of the linings. Concerning the latter two He said ﴿reclining on green cushions and beautiful rugs﴾. The "rafraf" has been explained as cushions and spreads, and explained as carpets, and explained as cushions above them.

According to every view, He did not describe them with what He described the carpets of the first two gardens.

Fifth: He said ﴿and the fruit of the two gardens is near﴾, meaning close and easy, which they reach however they wish. This is not mentioned concerning the latter two.

Sixth: He said ﴿in them are those restraining their gaze﴾.

That is, they have restricted their gaze to their husbands, so they see no one else, out of their contentment with them and their love for them. This implies that their beauty does not allow their husbands to look at anyone else.

He said concerning the latter two ﴿maidens restrained in pavilions﴾. And one who restricts her gaze to her husband by her own choice is more perfect than one who is restricted by other than herself.

Seventh: He described them as resembling rubies and coral in the purity of their color, its radiance and beauty, and this is not mentioned in those that follow.

Eighth: He, glorified and exalted, said concerning the first two gardens: ﴿Is the reward of good other than good?﴾ This requires that their people be of complete, absolute goodness, so their reward is of complete goodness.

Ninth: He began with describing the first two gardens and made them a reward for one who fears His standing. This indicates that they are the highest reward of the one who fears His standing. He ordered the mentioned reward upon fear, as an effect follows its cause. Since those who fear are of two types, the near ones and the people of the right hand, He mentioned the two gardens of the near ones, then mentioned the two gardens of the people of the right hand.

Tenth: He said ﴿and besides them two gardens﴾, and the context indicates that it is the opposite of "above," as al-Jawhari said.

If it is said: How are these four gardens distributed over one who fears the standing of his Lord?

It is said: Since those who fear are of two types as we have mentioned, the near ones have the two high gardens, and the people of the right hand have the two gardens below them. If it is said: Are the two gardens for the whole group of those who fear, sharing them, or does each one have two gardens, which are two orchards?

It is said: There are two views among the exegetes on this.

The second view is preferred for two reasons: one from transmission, and the second from meaning. As for the transmitted one, those who hold this view have related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "They are two orchards in the meadows of Paradise."

As for the one from meaning, one of the two gardens is the reward for performing the commands, and the second is the reward for avoiding the prohibitions.

If it is said: How, in mentioning the women, did He say "in them" in both places, while when He mentioned the others He said "in them" (dual)?

It is said: When He mentioned the cushions, after them He said ﴿in them are good, beautiful women﴾.

Then He repeated it in the latter two gardens with this wording, so that the wording and the meaning correspond, and Allah knows best.

(Section: on whether the believers among the jinn are in Paradise)

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens﴾

And He mentioned what is in the two gardens, up to His words: ﴿Neither man nor jinn has touched them before them﴾.

This indicates that the reward of the good among them is Paradise, in several respects:

First: "man" (min) is a word of generality, so it encompasses every one who fears.

Second: He ordered the mentioned reward upon fear of His standing, which shows that he deserves it by it. There has been disagreement over whether the idafah of "standing" to "Lord" is an idafah of the verbal noun to its subject or to its object, on two views: One is that the meaning is "and for him who fears his standing before his Lord," so on this it is an idafah of the verbal noun to its object.

The second is that the meaning is "and for him who fears the standing of his Lord over him and His watching over him," so it is an idafah of the verbal noun to its subject.

The two views are likewise in the words of the Exalted: ﴿But as for he who feared the standing of his Lord and restrained the soul from desire﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 40], and its parallel in His words: ﴿That is for him who fears My standing and fears My threat﴾ [Ibrahim: 14]. These are three places.

It may be said: The preferred one is the first, and that the meaning is "he feared his standing before his Lord," for several reasons:

One: The Qur'an's method in warning is to warn them of Allah and the Last Day. When He warns them of Him, He attaches the fear to Him, not to His standing over them, as in His words: ﴿So do not fear them, but fear Me﴾ [Al 'Imran: 175], and His words: ﴿That is for him who fears his Lord﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 8], and His words: ﴿They fear their Lord from above them﴾ [al-Nahl: 50], and His words: ﴿Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen, for them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [al-Mulk: 12]. In all of this He did not mention fear of His standing over them; rather He praised them for their fear and dread of Him.

Fear may also be mentioned attached to His punishment, as in His words: ﴿They hope for His mercy and fear His punishment﴾ [al-Isra': 57].

As for fear of His standing over them, although it is so, it is not the method of the Qur'an.

Two: This is parallel to His words: ﴿And warn with it those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 51]. Their fear of being gathered to Him is their fear of their standing before Him, and the Qur'an explains one part by another.

Three: The fear of a servant's standing before his Lord in the Hereafter is found only in one who believes in meeting Him, in the Last Day and in resurrection after death. This is what deserves the two mentioned gardens, for one does not believe in that with true belief except one who believes in the messengers, and it is from the belief in the unseen that the messengers brought.

As for Allah's standing over His servant in this world, His watching over him and His power over him, this is acknowledged by the believer and the disbeliever, the righteous and the wicked, and most of the disbelievers fear Allah's requital of them in this world, because they have witnessed the punishment of the wrongdoer for his wrong and the reward of the good for his goodness. But the servant's standing before his Lord in the Hereafter is not believed in except by the one who believes in the messengers.

If it is said: If the meaning is that he feared his Lord's standing over him in the Hereafter through requital, then both estimations are equal, so from where have you preferred one of them?

It is said: Warning with the servant's standing before his Lord is more forceful than warning with the Lord's standing over the servant, and for this He warned us in His words: ﴿The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 6]. Also, it is a specific standing, attributed to Allah, and that is on the Day of Resurrection, unlike Allah's standing over the servant, which is at every time. Moreover, Allah's power over the servant, His watching over him and His knowledge of him are not called "the standing of Allah," nor is this commonly used of the Lord.

Also, in the Qur'an and the Sunnah "maqam" is used only for a place, as in His words: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praised station﴾ [al-Isra': 79], and His words: ﴿How many gardens and springs and crops and a noble station did they leave behind﴾ [al-Dukhan: 25–26], and His words: ﴿Better in station and finer in assembly﴾ [Maryam: 73]. The point is that His words ﴿And for him who fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens﴾ encompass both categories, for several reasons, two of which were mentioned earlier:

Third: His words following this promise: ﴿Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾

Fourth: That He described their women as: ﴿Neither man nor jinn has touched them before them﴾ [al-Rahman: 56]. And this, Allah knows best, means that no man before them has touched the women of mankind, nor has any jinn before them touched the women of the jinn.

What shows that their reward is Paradise is His words: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—indeed, We do not allow to be lost the reward of one who does good work. Those will have gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow﴾ [al-Kahf: 30–31], and similar generalities.

It has been established that among them are believers, so they enter into the generality, just as their disbelievers enter among the disbelievers deserving the threat. The entry of their believers into the verses of promise is more fitting than the entry of their disbelievers into the verses of threat, for promise is His grace and threat is His justice, and His grace is from His mercy, which overcomes His wrath.

Also, the entry of their disobedient ones into the Fire was only because of their opposition to Allah's command; so when they obey Allah, they are admitted to Paradise. Also, there is no abode for the accountable other than Paradise and the Fire, and every accountable one who does not enter the Fire, Paradise is his abode.

Also, it has been established that when they answer the caller of Allah, He forgives them and protects them from His punishment, and everyone who is forgiven enters Paradise without doubt; the benefit of forgiveness is nothing but winning Paradise and being saved from the Fire. Also, it has been established that the Messenger was sent to them and that they are obligated to follow him, and that whoever of them obeys Allah and His Messenger is with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor, of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous, and excellent companions they are. As He said: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger—those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor, of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions﴾ [al-Nisa': 69]. He, glorified be He, has informed of His angels, the bearers of the Throne and those around it, that they seek forgiveness for those who believe, and that they say: ﴿So forgive those who repent and follow Your way and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire. Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them﴾ [Ghafir: 7–8].

This shows that every believer whom Allah forgives and whom He protects from the punishment of Hellfire has been promised Paradise. Belief, forgiveness of sin and protection from the Fire have been established for their believers, as mentioned, so their entry into Paradise is necessary, and Allah knows best.

And since their accountability has been established, with their division into Muslims, disbelievers, and righteous and below that, they are in the weighing in the manner of the human levels mentioned before, except that there is no messenger among them. The best of their ranks is the rank of the righteous, and if they had a higher rank than this, it would have been mentioned.

The Qur'an has indicated their division into three categories: righteous, those below them, and disbelievers.

Humankind surpasses them in the rank of messengership and prophethood, and the rank of those brought near, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 55, verse 54:

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And upon raised couches﴾.

So He described the couches as lined with silk brocade (istabraq). This indicates two matters.

The first: their outer surfaces (zahair) are higher and finer than their linings (batain), for their linings face the ground, while their outer surfaces are for beauty, adornment and direct contact.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Hubayra ibn Maryam, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding His saying: ﴿Their linings are of brocade﴾, that he said: "These linings, you have been informed of them; so how of the outer surfaces?"

The second: it indicates that they are lofty couches, having thickness and padding between the lining and the outer surface. Reports have been transmitted concerning their thickness and height, if they are preserved. The meaning is then the height of their place, as related by al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His saying: ﴿And upon raised couches﴾, that he said: "Their height is as the distance between the sky and the earth, and the journey between them is five hundred years."

Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the narration of Rushdin ibn Sa'd."

It has been said that its meaning is: the aforementioned height refers to the ranks (darajat) and the couches being upon them.

I say: Rushdin ibn Sa'd has munkar (rejected) narrations. Al-Daraqutni said: "He is not strong."

Ahmad said: "He does not care from whom he narrates. There is no harm in him regarding softening-of-hearts (raqa'iq) narrations." He also said: "I hope he is salih al-hadith (of sound narration)." Yahya ibn Ma'in said: "He is nothing." Abu Zur'a said: "He is weak."

Al-Jawzajani said: "He has munkar narrations; there is no doubt that he had poor memory. Therefore nothing that he alone narrates is relied upon."

Ibn Wahb said: "Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to us, from Darraj Abu al-Samh, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding His saying: ﴿And upon raised couches﴾, he said:

"The distance between the two couches is as the distance between the sky and the earth."

This is more likely to be the preserved version. And Allah knows best.

Al-Tabarani said: "Al-Miqdam ibn Dawud narrated to us, Asad ibn Musa narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Mutarrif ibn Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir, from Ka'b, regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And upon raised couches﴾, he said: "A journey of forty years." Al-Tabarani also said: "Ibrahim ibn Na'ila narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Amr al-Bajali narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umama, who said:

"The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the raised couches, and he said: 'If a couch were thrown from its top, it would fall to its base in a hundred autumns.'"

There is consideration regarding the raising (chain) of this hadith.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: "Ishaq ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, who said: I found in my father's book, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umama, regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And upon raised couches﴾, he said: 'If its uppermost part fell, it would not reach its lowest part after forty autumns.'"

(Section)

As for the couches, He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Reclining upon couches, their linings are of brocade﴾.

He said: ﴿And upon raised couches﴾. So He described the couches as lined with brocade, and this indicates two matters:

The first: their outer surfaces are higher and finer than their linings, for their linings are for the ground, while their outer surfaces are for beauty, adornment and direct contact.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Hubayra ibn Maryam, from Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud), regarding His saying ﴿Their linings are of brocade﴾, that he said: "These linings, you have been informed of them; so how of the outer surfaces?"
